title: Judicial Pardon
definition: Judicial Pardon is God's legal forgiveness of the believer's guilt on the basis of Christ's finished work.
summary: Judicial Pardon emphasizes God's legal declaration that the believer is no longer condemned.
christFocus: Jesus Christ secures pardon by bearing sin and standing as the believer's advocate.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content: Judicial pardon focuses on the courtroom aspect of salvation. God, the righteous Judge, does not ignore guilt; He pardons those in Christ because judgment has fallen on the Substitute. This doctrine gives legal certainty to forgiveness and assures the believer that condemnation has been answered at the cross.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content: This matters because many believers live as though their standing before God changes with every failure. Judicial pardon declares that the verdict in Christ is stronger than accusation. It guards assurance from being ruled by feelings, shame, or the enemy's charges.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Answer accusation with the finished work of Christ. Confess sin seriously, but do not return to a condemned identity. Encourage burdened believers with the truth that in Christ the Judge has spoken peace.
